name: 레우코스
type: Asteroid · Jupiter Trojan · L4 · D-type · Slow rotator
fact: One of the slowest-rotating bodies of its size known — a 446-hour (18.6-day) rotation period, unusually long for a 35-km asteroid. The slow spin suggests a complex collisional or tidal history with another body, possibly a recent (in geologic terms) major event.
bio: Discovered 1997, named for Leucus (a comrade of Odysseus, killed at Troy). D-type spectral classification — the darkest and reddest of the Trojan family. Lucy's 2028-04-18 encounter will profile shape, surface composition, and the rotation-state evolution behind the slow spin.
